thread:
sam: Kicking off canary for api-gateway v2.8.0 -> global. Rolling 5% to canary. Primary SLOs: p99 < 400ms, 429s < 0.2%.

deploy-bot: Canary launched: id=canary-4567891234 target=api-gateway:v2.8.0 traffic=5% strategy=linear-5min. Dashboard: https://deploys.redwood.internal/canary/4567891234 :robot_face:

matt: Heads up — watch auth and rate-limiter metrics closely. v2.8.0 changed default token bucket refill for bursty clients.

ana: Observability: initial p99 stable, but I’m seeing a small 429 uptick on edge-rate-limiter for the canary nodes (~0.12% -> 0.4%). Not yet at auto-pause threshold but trending.

jen: I'm pulling request traces. 429s are concentrated on a handful of client IDs hitting short-interval bursts. Could be refill interval mismatch.

sam: Ops-bot, can you snapshot rate-limiter config for canary vs baseline?

ops-bot: Config diff: api-gateway:v2.7.9 -> token_bucket.refill_ms=1000, v2.8.0 -> token_bucket.refill_ms=250 (intent: lower latency for small bursts).

matt: That refill delta is likely the culprit — more frequent, smaller refills causing token starvation for aggregated proxies. If 429 > 1% sustained 2m we pause. No auto-rollforward.

ana: Can we try a runtime override on canary to set refill_ms back to 1000? Quick config patch applied: token_bucket.refill_ms=1000 on canary nodes. Watching.

observability-bot: Metrics update: canary-4567891234 429_rate dropped from 0.38% -> 0.09% within 90s after config change. p99 unchanged.

jen: That looks good. Recommend keep canary paused and run a 20m soak to validate before resuming rollout. Also note for release notes: changed default refill_ms caused regression for certain aggregated proxies; recommend explicit config until next patch.

matt: Agreed. Pause traffic, soak 20m. Sam, add an action item to pin v2.7.9 for customers using aggregated proxies or provide the config override in docs.

sam: Added ticket INF-789 to backlog and draft release note: "Behavior change: token_bucket.refill_ms default lowered in v2.8.0; can cause higher 429s for proxied burst patterns. Interim: set token_bucket.refill_ms=1000." PR: https://git.redwood/release-notes/PR-1400

deploy-bot: Canary paused (traffic -> 0%). Soak timer started (20m). canary_state=PAUSED id=canary-4567891234.

matt: Next steps: after soak if stable we can proceed with a second canary that ships v2.8.0 + config default restored, or roll back to v2.7.9 and pin. Prefer targeted second canary to validate behavior with default restored.

ana: I'll open a quick hotfix branch to revert the refill default and run CI. Also pushing a monitoring rule that flags 429 spikes on aggregated-proxy labels.

jen: I'll update CS and account managers that a temporary config may be required for customers behind proxies.

sam: Will post final decision here after soak. Thanks everyone.
